parakeet: Christianity doesn't just shape what people believe. It shapes how they believe. It trains the mind to prioritize loyalty over logic, emotion over evidence, and predetermined conclusions over genuine inquiry. This isn't a childish misunderstanding. It is a lifelong epistemological system that governs identity, politics, relationships, and meaning making. When you look at these six templates together, the moral template, the love template, the self-worth template, the emotional template, the belonging template, and the epistemological template, a picture emerges. Christianity doesn't just shape private belief. It shapes public behavior. It shapes relational patterns. It shapes institutional cultures. It shapes politics. It shapes entire generations of psychological reflexes. Because once a system teaches you that authority defines goodness, love requires surrender. Selfhood is defective. Guilt is righteous. Belonging is fragile. And thinking for yourself is dangerous. You don't just leave those ideas behind. You carry their fingerprints into adulthood, into parenting, into relationships, into voting booths, into workplaces, into every version of yourself you become. But here's the part that matters most. None of these patterns are you. They were installed, so they can be uninstalled, and they can be replaced with frameworks that are humane, rational, relationally healthy, and grounded in actual well-being.
